description: REQ-106's own text specifies exactly ONE evaluation point for BOTH kill-switches (`evaluateColdStartKillSwitch` and, new this revision, `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch`): 'BEFORE acquiring the `loan_${lenderId}` lock' (behavioral-spec.md:711-713 and the two Edge Cases at :1311-1320: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse BEFORE ever acquiring the lock'). But THIS SAME revision's own dual-lock design (added for FIND-401) explicitly requires a SEPARATE, later, lock-protected FRESH read of `loans.jsonl`, taken only AFTER both locks are held, that re-evaluates REQ-102(a)-(d), REQ-101's availability, and 'REQ-104/105 sizing' (behavioral-spec.md:980-983: 'SHALL... take a FRESH read of `loans.jsonl` and RE-EVALUATE REQ-102's own conditions (a)-(d)... BEFORE proceeding to REQ-101's own availability recheck, REQ-104/105 sizing, `n = nextLoanSequenceForLender(...)`'). The critical-section ordering the Acceptance Criteria give explicitly (behavioral-spec.md:1344-1349: 'a FRESH read of `loans.jsonl` -> REQ-102(a)-(c) re-check -> REQ-101 read/re-check -> REQ-104/105 compute -> `n = nextLoanSequenceForLender(...)` -> disbursement transfer -> ... append') never lists EITHER kill-switch as part of that lock-protected, fresh-read sequence. So while `countSuccessfulOnTimeRepayments`/`computeLoanCapUsd` (the SIZING half of 'REQ-105') get recomputed against the fresh, lock-protected read, `computeColdStartRepaymentRate`/`evaluateColdStartKillSwitch` (the PAUSE half of the SAME 'REQ-105') and `computeOverallDefaultRateUsd`/`evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch` (REQ-114) do NOT -- both are evaluated exactly once, on an OLDER, non-lock-protected snapshot taken before either lock exists. Because these two monitors are COLONY-WIDE (not scoped to the specific lender or borrower whose locks are held), this is not closed by the per-lender/per-borrower locking REQ-106 otherwise relies on: two concurrent issuance attempts for TWO DIFFERENT lenders and TWO DIFFERENT borrowers (REQ-106's own Edge Case at :1255-1259 explicitly says these proceed with ZERO lock contention between them) can each independently read the SAME pre-pause `loanRows` snapshot, each see `paused:false`, and both proceed to disburse -- even in the exact window where a just-landed large default should be tripping REQ-114's own 'colony-wide... systemic risk-mitigation trigger' (behavioral-spec.md:855-857) and refusing 'ANY new loan' (:853). This is structurally the SAME class of TOCTOU race FIND-401 already found and closed for borrower eligibility ('this window is not merely a millisecond-scale race: it can persist for an ARBITRARY duration', :972-973) -- but the fix (a fresh, lock-protected re-check) was applied only to REQ-101/102/105-sizing, never to either kill-switch's own pause DECISION. The proof obligations codify this gap rather than catching it: PROP-105h (verification-architecture.md:130) and PROP-114c (verification-architecture.md:133) both require ONLY that the real code 'imports and calls' the relevant kill-switch function 'BEFORE acquiring the `loan_${lenderId}` lock' -- neither requires the call to use the FRESH, lock-protected read, and neither Gate item (2) (behavioral-spec review Gate, verification-architecture.md:252-285) nor any Tier-2 proof obligation in the 149-row table tests a scenario where a kill-switch's pause state changes between two concurrent, non-lock-contending issuance attempts. An implementation built exactly to this spec's own acceptance criteria would satisfy every stated proof obligation while still allowing a burst of unrelated, concurrent large-loan issuances to slip past a just-tripped colony-wide default kill-switch.

evidence.snippet: SHALL... take a FRESH read of `loans.jsonl` and RE-EVALUATE REQ-102's own conditions (a)-(d) for this borrower against that fresh read BEFORE proceeding to REQ-101's own availability recheck, REQ-104/105 sizing, `n = nextLoanSequenceForLender(...)`, and disbursement ... [Edge Case] ANY loan request ... is evaluated while REQ-114's `evaluateOverallDefaultKillSwitch` returns `paused:true`: THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse BEFORE ever acquiring the `loan_${lenderId}` lock ... [Acceptance Criteria] The loan-issuance critical section (a FRESH read of `loans.jsonl` -> REQ-102(a)-(c) re-check -> REQ-101 read/re-check -> REQ-104/105 compute -> `n = nextLoanSequenceForLender(...)` -> disbursement transfer -> ...)

crossCheck.note: PROP-105h and PROP-114c each require only a control-flow read confirming the real issuance code calls the respective kill-switch function 'BEFORE acquiring the `loan_${lenderId}` lock' -- neither requires (nor tests) that the call use the SAME fresh, lock-protected read REQ-106's own cross-lender-exclusion mechanism established for REQ-101/102/105-sizing. No PROP in the table exercises two concurrent, non-lock-contending (different lender AND different borrower) issuance attempts racing against a kill-switch state transition.
